taunt: Two sporks. One string. Zero mercy.
I am the fast one. The possum timed me with a sundial.
Anchovies are a vegetable. Hold still while I explain.
I have never hit myself with these. Today is not the day. Probably.
The string is a shoelace. The shoe is still in the dumpster.
Spork one is for soup. Spork two is for you.
I got the spork. Lidd got the lid. I won.
Three tines left. I lost the fourth in a fight with a sandwich.
You blinked. I hit you four times. Blink again.
Fast is a lifestyle. You picked the other one.
My hat is paper. My elbows are not.
I eat anchovies off the floor of the pipe. I fear nothing.
Keep up. No, you cannot. That was a trick.
The possum says I talk too fast. The possum says I hit too fast. The possum naps.
You have one face. I have two sporks. Math.
I would give you a head start, but I already finished.
I tied these myself. The knot is a mystery. Even to me.
Spork means spoon and fork. Together they mean trouble.
Napkin says I am annoying. Napkin says four words a year. Two of them were about me.
This hat came with a milkshake. The milkshake was not mine.
You swing like you are paid by the hour.
I can run on walls. For a second. Then I hit people.
The sporks are plastic. Plastic lasts forever. So will this.
I lick the sporks between hits. Hygiene is for the slow.
I was a utensil. Now I am a problem.
Dodge this. No? Okay. Dodge the next one. No? Wow.
Anchovy breath is a weapon. I have two others.
I have a tail and two sporks. That is three things to hit you with.
The lunch lady banned me. The ban did not say anything about this.
Strawe shoots from far away. I do not have the patience.
I ran here. I will run back. In between, you.
Skipped the warm-up. Skipped the stretch. Did not skip you.
You are slow in a way that feels on purpose.
The sensei said use the sporks wisely. I use them often. Close enough.
The shoelace has a knot for every fight. There is no room left.
I jumped over a rat today. The rat was bigger than you. Louder too.
You are the kind of person who orders plain cheese. I can smell it.
The hat stays on. The hat has always stayed on. Ask anyone.
Hands up. Sporks up. One of us is ready.
I fight like I eat. Too fast and with my mouth open.
The pipe echoes. So will this.
I have been up since the anchovies. That was Tuesday.
Catch me. You cannot. Catch this. You will.
There is a fourth tine out there somewhere. I hit someone with it.
The possum calls me Sporke. Lidd calls me late. Napkin calls me nothing.
I spin the sporks for fun. The fun is yours. The sporks are mine.
You have the reflexes of a wet napkin. Not our Napkin. A regular one.
I am sixteen in gecko years. In spork years I am brand new.
Lunch rush. You are the rush.
Fast food. That is me. I am the fast. You are the food.
Nobody expects the soup spoon to hurt. The fork half does the work.
I swallowed a tine once. It came back. Everything comes back down here.
I can do a flip. Lidd cannot. Do not tell him I told you.
You fight like a vending machine. Slow, and the snack is bad.
The string snapped once. I caught both sporks. In my teeth.
Move faster. No. Faster. You are not trying.
I named the sporks. Spork and Also Spork.
My hat has a stripe. The stripe is ketchup. It was always ketchup.
I hit first, second, third and fourth. You get fifth.
Anchovies, extra. On the pizza. On the tray. On you.
I am made of elbows and apologies. No apologies today.
You run like the rent is paid. Mine is not.
The possum says hit low. I say hit often. We are both right.
I counted your hits. One. I counted mine. I lost count.
The sewer has a speed limit. I am the reason.
Lidd has a tray. Napkin has a mop. I have two sporks and a plan. The plan is sporks.
I licked a subway rail on a dare. Your punch is not scary.
Your stance is a suggestion. My sporks are a decision.
Faster than a rat with a slice. Ask the rat.
The hat is not a mask. I know. The possum did not.
My tail got caught in the string once. We do not talk about it.
Every spork has a story. These two are the same story. It is you.
I have energy for this. I have energy for everything. That is the problem.
Watch the hands. No, the other hands. There are only two. Confusing, right?
I was going to take this slow. I do not know how.
Still here? I left and came back. Twice.
Anchovies taste like the sea. The sea is a sewer with ambition.
I spin. You spin. Only one of us meant to.
You moved. Rude. I was aiming there.
The spork is the perfect weapon. Stabs, scoops, and fits in a pocket.
I would trash talk more, but my mouth cannot keep up with my feet.
You hit like a paper hat. Mine is tougher.
I beat Lidd in a race. He said it was not a race. It was a race.
Try to grab me. Napkin tries every day. Napkin has zero geckos.
The sporks are plastic, the lace is cotton, and your odds are nothing.
You are large and slow. I am neither. Guess how this goes.
One spork is bent. It still works. So does my elbow.
I bite when the sporks are tangled. They are tangled a lot.
I am the only gecko who can eat and fight at the same time. Watch.
I beat the possum once. He was asleep. It counts.
You call that a dodge? I call that a tour.
Second slice goes to whoever is standing. Guess.
Dinner is at six. You are dinner. It is five fifty-nine.
I run laps around the pipe before breakfast. You are my breakfast lap.
My hat says SODA. The possum could not read it. I can.
I do not block. Blocking is for geckos with time.
Nobody has ever told me to slow down and lived to say it twice.
This is my resting speed.
You should see me after sugar. You will not. You will be down.
Four geckos, one string, two sporks. I got the good bag.
continue: Anchovies are a vegetable. Put in a coin and I will prove it.
Lidd said pineapple. I said anchovies. The coin decides.
Napkin wants olives on the continue screen. Coin, before he folds.
Extra anchovies or I stay down. Those are the terms.
One coin and the anchovy question goes to a vote. I vote twice.
I am not dead. I am waiting for the toppings to be fair.
Strawe put sauce on my sporks. Coin so I can get up and say something.
Insert a coin. Anchovies are the only topping that fights back.
The possum says a coin is a coin. The possum does not like anchovies. Coin anyway.
Ten seconds. Pick anchovies. Pick a coin. Pick both.
You cannot continue without picking a side. Anchovies. Coin.
Half anchovy, half more anchovy. One coin.
I will get up for a quarter and a fish.
Pineapple is a fruit. Anchovies are a vegetable. Coin, and I will explain the fish part.
Whoever pays picks the topping. I have nothing. I have sporks. Coin.
ending: Sporke tied a third spork to the string. The possum said no. He did it anyway.
Sporke won the toppings vote with anchovies. The other three ate the crust and nothing else.
Sporke ran a lap of the city during the credits. He came back before the names finished.
The fourth tine turned up in Napkin's mop. Nobody said anything. Sporke said plenty.
Sporke finally hit himself with the sporks. He said it did not count. It counted.
The paper hat got wet in the sewer and stayed on. Health code now covers it.
Sporke taught Kevin the rat to spin a spork. Kevin is better at it.
The shoelace broke in the last fight. Sporke found the shoe. It fit.
Sporke beat 996 bootlegs and still cannot sit still for the credits. He is reading them from the ceiling.
The possum timed Sporke with a sundial again. It was night. Sporke won anyway.
Sporke opened a spork stand in the pipe. One item on the menu. It is a spork.
Lidd got the corner slice. Sporke got there first and licked it. Everyone ate around it.
